INTRODUCTION.title: Welcome
INTRODUCTION.body:
Welcome to the BA Autopilot tutorial. It starts with a brief introduction to Barbarian Assault, then explains how the plugin works. Use Next and Back to move through it.

BA Autopilot is still being tested: there may be bugs, and some mechanics may not work reliably yet. Feel free to join our Discord to give feedback and suggestions. The link is at the top left of the BA Autopilot panel (click the BA Autopilot button in RuneLite's sidebar to open it).

BA Autopilot guides your actions, one step at a time. It never clicks or does anything automatically: you are always the one who plays.

INTRODUCTION.title: Your team
INTRODUCTION.body: Barbarian Assault is played by a team of five. Each player has a role: Attacker, Defender, Collector or Healer.

INTRODUCTION.title: Team setups
INTRODUCTION.body: One role is doubled. Teams usually run two Attackers (as shown) or two Healers. A single Healer can struggle, but so can a single weak Attacker: the right setup depends on the players.

INTRODUCTION.title: Changing roles
INTRODUCTION.body: Roles can change between waves. A team might start with two Attackers and switch to two Healers for the last few waves.

INTRODUCTION.title: Ten waves
INTRODUCTION.body: Barbarian Assault is played in ten waves. Waves 1 to 9 play the same way, each one harder than the last.

INTRODUCTION.title: The Penance
INTRODUCTION.body: Every wave, four kinds of Penance come at the team: Fighters, Rangers, Runners and Healers.

INTRODUCTION.title: The Queen
INTRODUCTION.body: Wave 10 starts like the others, but once all its Penance are dead, the Penance Queen appears. *Defeat her to finish the run.*

BASICS.title: Finding a team
BASICS.body:
Before any wave you need a team of five players. Teams form here, in room 1 of the lobby, where you are now.

If you're looking for a team, type the role you want in the chat, for example "Def" for Defender, or "Coll or Atk" if you'd play Collector or Attacker.

Teams that are missing a player say what they need: "Need atk" means they need an Attacker, and "Atk2go" means they're ready to go once an Attacker joins. When a team needs your role, reply to them, and their leader sends you an invite.

BASICS.title: Joining a team
BASICS.body: The team's leader sends you an invite. Pick your role in it and confirm to join.

BASICS.title: Leading a team
BASICS.body: To lead, take a scroll from the table, use it on each player, and confirm the role they picked.

BASICS.title: Starting a wave
BASICS.body: Once the team is ready, the leader climbs down the ladder to start the wave. The leader does this for the first wave and for every wave after it.

BASICS.title: If someone leaves
BASICS.body: If a player leaves the team after wave 1, the run can't carry on. Come back to room 1's door, right-click the entrance and choose to reset the wave: the team can then start again from the beginning.

BASICS.title: Inside a wave
BASICS.body:
When the leader climbs down the ladder, the whole team is taken into the arena, and the wave begins.

Every player starts the wave with a horn in their inventory. A role panel also appears on your screen: it shows your role, the time left before the next call, the call you have to make, and the call you heard from your partner.

BASICS.title: The arena: waves 1 to 9
BASICS.body:
Penance come out of the caves along the north wall. The traps are on the west and east sides, and the egg launchers and hoppers stand on two hills. The hills are safer: Penance can't go up them, though Rangers can still shoot you there. The Healer spring and the dispensers are by the south wall.

This is just a first look at the arena: each of these places is explained on the pages that follow.

BASICS.title: The arena: wave 10
BASICS.body: Wave 10 has a single egg launcher, and adds poison and lava craters and petrified mushrooms for the Queen's eggs. The Queen appears in the middle.

BASICS.title: The horn
BASICS.body:
Every 30 seconds, each player gets a new call to make, shown in their role's panel. Right-click the horn in your inventory and pick that Tell- option to send it to your partner. "Collector: Red eggs!" tells the Collector which eggs to pick up.

BA Autopilot makes this easier: it colours the right Tell- option green in the horn's menu.

BASICS.title: Partners
BASICS.body: Calls go both ways between partners: Attackers and Collectors call each other, and so do Defenders and Healers. Each call tells the partner what to use.

BASICS.title: Roles in battle
BASICS.body: In a wave, Attackers kill the Fighters and Rangers, the Defender traps the Runners, the Healer poisons the Penance Healers and keeps the team alive, and the Collector gathers the eggs. The next pages cover each role in turn.

BASICS.title: Attacker: the call
BASICS.body: The Collector calls what the Penance are weak to, in three forms at once: a melee style, an arrow and a spell, such as Accurate/Field/Water. Use the one that fits your weapon.

BASICS.title: Attacker: weapons
BASICS.body: *Ranged is the strongest style, and the best choice for new players:* switch to the arrows the call names. Melee is used only in very advanced play, and magic is basically not used in BA.

BASICS.title: Attacker: Fighters
BASICS.body: Attackers kill Penance Fighters, using the attack style the Collector calls.

BASICS.title: Attacker: Rangers
BASICS.body: Rangers attack from a distance. Attackers kill them the same way, with the called style.

BASICS.title: Defender: Runners
BASICS.body: Runners try to escape. The Defender lures them onto the trap with the bait the Healer calls, and the trap kills them. After two kills the trap breaks, and the Defender fixes it with logs and a hammer.

BASICS.title: Healer: Penance Healers
BASICS.body: Penance Healers can heal the Runners.

BASICS.title: Healer: poisoning
BASICS.body: The Healer kills them with poisoned food: the kind the Defender calls. With several about, go between them, feeding each in turn.

BASICS.title: Collector: eggs
BASICS.body: Dead Penance drop eggs. The Collector picks up the colour the Attacker calls.

BASICS.title: The egg launcher
BASICS.body:
After collecting eggs, the Collector loads them into the egg launcher. The Collector, or any teammate, can then fire them to help kill the Penance.

There's no aiming: you pick the kind of Penance, and the launcher picks which one to hit. Whoever fires, aim in this order: red at Runners, red at Healers, green at Runners, then green at Healers.

BA Autopilot outlines that button in the launcher window and crosses out the stun buttons.

BASICS.title: Egg types
BASICS.body:
Red eggs deal 3 damage, and 0-1 to Penance within 3 tiles.

Green eggs deal 1 and poison for 5 more.

Blue eggs stun: the Penance can't move, but it can't be attacked either, which only slows the team down. Blue eggs are basically not used.

BASICS.title: The Healer spring
BASICS.body:
The Healer watches the team's health.

To heal teammates, use the vial on the Healer spring to fill it, then use it on them.

The Healer can also drink from the spring to heal itself.

BASICS.title: Eggs for the Queen: C-H-A-D-C
BASICS.body: Once the Queen appears, the team passes each of her eggs around in a fixed order: Collector, Healer, Attacker, Defender, and back to the Collector. Players remember it as CHAD C. Each player works on the egg, then hands it to the next.

BASICS.title: C: Collector
BASICS.body: Yellow eggs appear at random on the ground around the Queen. The Collector picks them up and passes them to the Healer.

BASICS.title: H: Healer
BASICS.body: The Healer poisons the egg by using it on a poison crater.

BASICS.title: A: Attacker
BASICS.body: The Attacker gets spikes from a petrified mushroom and adds them to the egg.

BASICS.title: D: Defender
BASICS.body: The Defender heats the egg by using it on a lava crater, making an omega egg.

BASICS.title: C: Collector
BASICS.body: The Collector takes the omega egg back to load it.

BASICS.title: Defeating the Queen
BASICS.body: Weapons can't hurt the Queen. The Collector loads the omega eggs into the egg hopper, and teammates fire them at her from the egg launcher.

BASICS.title: Spamming omegas
BASICS.body:
A common strategy is to stack: everyone whose eggs are done stands at the cannon.

Clicking the preloaded cannon opens its aiming window, where the Omega button shows 0, because no omega egg is loaded yet. The players keep clicking that button over and over: this is called *spamming* it.

Meanwhile, the Collector loads the omega eggs one at a time: click one omega egg in the inventory, then click the hopper. Clicking the hopper on its own loads all the eggs at once, which is not what you want here.

Why spam? As soon as an egg is loaded, every player clicking the button fires it, so one egg hits the Queen several times. Eight hits finish her, so the team needs far fewer omega eggs.

BASICS.title: Dispensers
BASICS.body: Next to the Healer spring stand the dispensers, one for each role. Players stock up at theirs at the start of a wave, and restock during it.

BASICS.title: Attacker dispenser
BASICS.body: Attackers take arrows or runes here.

BASICS.title: Defender dispenser
BASICS.body:
Defenders take bait here: crackers, tofu or worms.

Stock-Up takes all three kinds of bait in one click, so you're ready for any call.

BASICS.title: Healer dispenser
BASICS.body:
Healers take vials and poisoned food here: tofu, worms or meat.

Stock-Up takes all three poisoned foods in one click, so you're ready for any call.

BASICS.title: Collector Converter
BASICS.body: From Collector level 2, the Collector can convert eggs here: green to red, red to green, and blue to green. Some eggs break: 25% convert at level 2, up to 85% at level 5.

BASICS.title: That's the basics
BASICS.body: You now know how a Barbarian Assault run works: the team, the calls, the Penance, the eggs and the Queen. The next tutorials cover one role each, in CHAD order: Collector, Healer, Attacker and Defender, and how BA Autopilot guides you through it, step by step.

COLLECTOR.title: The Collector
COLLECTOR.body:
When Penance die, they drop eggs. As the Collector, you pick up the eggs of the colour the Attacker calls and load them into the egg launchers, so the team can fire them. You also tell the Attacker which style to use.

BA Autopilot shows you one step at a time: which eggs to pick up, when to load them, and when to fire. It colours the right call green in your horn's menu.

COLLECTOR.title: The BA Autopilot overlay
COLLECTOR.body:
This is the BA Autopilot overlay. It shows the one thing to do now. You can move it by holding Alt and dragging it.

The coloured tag shows what kind of step it is. Under it are your call, the call you heard, and the time left before the next call.

COLLECTOR.title: Your call
COLLECTOR.body:
Every 30 seconds, the Attacker needs a new call from you: which style to use. When it's time, your game view turns red. That's your signal.

*Stop whatever you're doing.* Right-click your horn and pick the Tell- option that BA Autopilot colours green. The red goes away once you've called.

COLLECTOR.title: Opening: the west route
COLLECTOR.body:
At the start of each wave, walk around the west cannon hill to reach the Attackers. Don't wait for a call to start walking.

The route is drawn on the floor for you: follow it, and stop on the marked tile at its end.

COLLECTOR.title: Picking up eggs
COLLECTOR.body:
Only pick up eggs of the colour the Attacker called. A wrong egg explodes and hurts you.

Every egg of the called colour gets a dot. A green dot means a left-click on it picks it up. A yellow dot means another item is on top of it: right-click that spot and choose Take on the called egg.

BA Autopilot marks the tile of the next egg to pick up. It prefers eggs you can left-click, unless they are much further away.

COLLECTOR.title: Your egg bag
COLLECTOR.body:
Your first eggs go into the collection bag in your inventory, so they don't take up any inventory slots. You don't need to do anything for this: it happens when you pick them up.

The overlay counts the eggs in your bag and in your inventory together, on the line called Carrying.

COLLECTOR.title: Loading the hopper
COLLECTOR.body:
To load, click the hopper next to the egg launcher. One click loads every egg you carry into it, from your bag and your inventory.

*Load as soon as the overlay asks you to:* your team can only fire the eggs that are in the hopper.

COLLECTOR.title: Blue eggs
COLLECTOR.body:
Blue eggs stun the Penance, which doesn't really help your team, so there's no real need for them. Pick them up when blue is called: that still counts.

Loading blue eggs into the hopper is fine, and it's a quick way to free up inventory space. You can also destroy them: when you need the space, the overlay asks you to. Right-click a blue egg in your inventory and choose Destroy, or shift-click it.

COLLECTOR.title: Firing the launcher
COLLECTOR.body:
If a Runner is escaping, the overlay might guide you to the egg launcher, to help bring it down.

Click the launcher to open its window. BA Autopilot outlines the best button to click, and crosses out the stun buttons you should never use.

COLLECTOR.title: Waiting for eggs
COLLECTOR.body:
When there's nothing to pick up, the overlay asks you to wait near the Attackers.

Eggs drop where Fighters and Rangers die, so new eggs will appear close to you.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: before the Queen
COLLECTOR.body:
In wave 10, eggs don't give points. They're still useful, though: load a few to help bring down the Runners and Penance Healers.

Make sure at least one egg stays loaded in the cannon for the Queen. This is called *preloading*: with an egg loaded, your teammates can aim at the Queen as soon as she appears. BA Autopilot tells you when to do it.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: make room
COLLECTOR.body:
Once every Penance is dead and an egg is preloaded, the other eggs you carry are no use any more.

You'll need the space for the Queen's yellow eggs, so the overlay asks you to destroy them. Right-click an egg in your inventory and choose Destroy, or shift-click it.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: yellow eggs
COLLECTOR.body:
Only omega eggs can hurt the Queen, and every omega egg starts as a yellow egg. When the Queen appears, yellow eggs drop around her.

The overlay asks you to pick up 5 of them first. These 5 are your first batch: the next pages show what happens to them.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: the egg chain
COLLECTOR.body:
A yellow egg goes round the team before it can hurt the Queen. You pass it to the Healer, who poisons it. The Attacker adds spikes, and the Defender heats it into an omega egg.

The omega egg then comes back to you, ready to load into the cannon. Players call this order CHAD: Collector, Healer, Attacker, Defender.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: passing the batch
COLLECTOR.body:
Once you have 5 yellow eggs, the overlay asks you to pass them to the Healer. The Healer is marked for you.

To pass an egg, click a yellow egg in your inventory, then click the Healer. Do this once for each egg.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: collecting the reserve
COLLECTOR.body:
After you pass the first 5 yellow eggs, the overlay asks you to pick up 3 more. These 3 eggs are the *reserve*.

The reserve is there in case the first 5 omega eggs aren't enough to kill the Queen. If your team stacks properly at the cannon (explained a few pages on), each egg can hit the Queen several times, so fewer eggs are needed and the reserve might not be used at all.

Pick them up the same way as before: click each marked yellow egg on the ground.

You can change both numbers. To open the panel, click the BA Autopilot button in RuneLite's sidebar. On the Collector card, set Queen yellow batch (the first batch) and Queen reserve eggs (the reserve).

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: holding the reserve
COLLECTOR.body:
Keep the 3 reserve eggs in your inventory. Don't pass them to the Healer yet: the first 5 omega eggs may be enough to kill the Queen on their own, especially if your team stacks properly at the cannon.

If the Queen is still alive after the first 5 omega eggs have been fired, the overlay asks you to pass the reserve to the Healer. Pass them the same way as the first batch: click a yellow egg, then click the Healer.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: loading omegas
COLLECTOR.body:
The finished omega eggs come back to you from the Defender. You load them into the hopper one at a time. The overlay first marks a tile two tiles south of the hopper: stand there.

To load one egg, click an omega egg in your inventory, then click the hopper. *Don't just click the hopper:* that loads all of them at once.

COLLECTOR.title: Wave 10: spamming omegas
COLLECTOR.body:
Many teams stack at the cannon: they wait there and keep clicking the Omega button, *spamming* it, so each omega egg is fired as soon as you load it.

Why is spamming useful? When several players fire the same loaded egg, that one egg can hit the Queen several times. That reduces the total number of omega eggs your team needs.

Loading one at a time is on by default: it's One omega at a time, in the Advanced part of the Collector card. If your whole team stacks, also tell BA Autopilot: click the BA Autopilot button in RuneLite's sidebar, open the General & display section, and turn on Team stacks at Queen cannon. Your teammates' overlays then send them to the cannon once their eggs are done.

COLLECTOR.title: Collector: done
COLLECTOR.body: That's the Collector. Click Healer > to continue with the Healer tutorial.

HEALER.title: The Healer
HEALER.body:
As the Healer, you poison the Penance Healers with the food the Defender calls, and you heal your teammates with the vial. You also tell the Defender which bait the Runners want.

BA Autopilot shows you one step at a time: which food to use and on which Penance Healer, when to restock, and who to heal. It colours the right call green in your horn's menu.

HEALER.title: The BA Autopilot overlay
HEALER.body:
This is the BA Autopilot overlay. It shows the one thing to do now. You can move it by holding Alt and dragging it.

The coloured tag shows what kind of step it is. Under it are your call, the call you heard, and the time left before the next call.

HEALER.title: Your call
HEALER.body:
Every 30 seconds, the Defender needs a new call from you: which bait the Runners want. When it's time, your game view turns red. That's your signal.

*Stop whatever you're doing.* Right-click your horn and pick the Tell- option that BA Autopilot colours green. The red goes away once you've called.

HEALER.title: Opening: Stock-Up
HEALER.body: Start every wave at your dispenser. Click it once: its left-click is Stock-Up, which gives you all three kinds of poisoned food in one go.

HEALER.title: Opening: the healer spawn
HEALER.body:
Then walk to where the Penance Healers come out, and wait there for the Defender's call.

The call tells you which food the Penance Healers want. Don't feed them before it comes.

HEALER.title: Poison outlines
HEALER.body:
Each Penance Healer is outlined by its poison: green while it's fresh, then light green, yellow and orange as it fades, and red when it has none, because it was never fed or the poison wore off. Feed the red ones first.

BA Autopilot marks the one to feed next: it gets a thicker outline and a FEED badge above its head, with the food to use. The overlay names it too, so you can simply follow it.

HEALER.title: Feeding
HEALER.body:
To feed a Penance Healer, click the called food in your inventory (it's outlined), then click the Penance Healer.

The overlay may ask you to feed the same Penance Healer again: that brings it down quicker.

HEALER.title: The healer table
HEALER.body:
At the bottom of the overlay, you can see each Penance Healer's food and poison, how full your vial is, and your two most hurt teammates.

You don't need to act on this: the overlay already tells you what to do next.

HEALER.title: Keeping food
HEALER.body:
You need food for the Penance Healers that haven't come out yet.

When you're running low, the overlay sends you back to your dispenser for more. Right-click the dispenser and pick the Take- option for the food it names. Its left-click, Stock-Up, takes all three.

HEALER.title: Healing teammates
HEALER.body:
To fill your vial, click the vial in your inventory, then click the Healer spring.

To heal a teammate, click the vial, then click the teammate that the overlay names.

HEALER.title: Staying alive
HEALER.body:
Only you, the Healer, can drink from the spring. When your own health is low, the overlay sends you there first.

Click the spring to drink from it, then go back to what the overlay tells you.

HEALER.title: Wave 10: poisoning eggs
HEALER.body:
In wave 10, the Collector passes you yellow eggs. To poison one, click the yellow egg in your inventory, then click a poison crater. *Don't click the crater on its own.*

Then pass the poisoned egg to the Attacker: click it in your inventory, then click the Attacker.

HEALER.title: Wave 10: by the spring
HEALER.body: Between eggs, stay by the Healer spring. Hurt teammates can come to you there, and you can refill your vial right away.

HEALER.title: Healer: done
HEALER.body: That's the Healer. Click Attacker > to continue with the Attacker tutorial.

ATTACKER.title: The Attacker
ATTACKER.body:
As the Attacker, you kill the Penance Fighters and Rangers, using the style the Collector calls. You also tell the Collector which eggs to pick up.

BA Autopilot shows you one step at a time: which arrows to wield, who to attack, and when to stop. It colours the right call green in your horn's menu.

ATTACKER.title: The BA Autopilot overlay
ATTACKER.body:
This is the BA Autopilot overlay. It shows the one thing to do now. You can move it by holding Alt and dragging it.

The coloured tag shows what kind of step it is. Under it are your call, the call you heard, and the time left before the next call.

ATTACKER.title: Your call
ATTACKER.body:
Every 30 seconds, the Collector needs a new call from you: which eggs to pick up. When it's time, your game view turns red. That's your signal.

*Stop whatever you're doing.* Right-click your horn and pick the Tell- option that BA Autopilot colours green. The red goes away once you've called.

ATTACKER.title: Opening: arrows
ATTACKER.body:
Start at your dispenser and take all four types of arrows. Right-click the dispenser to see each type, and take every one.

With all four in your inventory, you can switch as soon as the Collector calls.

ATTACKER.title: Opening: route and wait tile
ATTACKER.body:
Walk around the west cannon hill to reach the caves. The route is drawn on the floor for you.

Then stand on the marked tile by the caves and wait for the first Fighter or Ranger.

ATTACKER.title: The called arrows
ATTACKER.body:
When the Collector calls, wield the arrows the call names. They're outlined in green in your inventory.

To wield them, click the outlined arrows.

ATTACKER.title: Attacking
ATTACKER.body: Click the outlined Penance to attack it. The overlay keeps you on the same one until it dies, so you don't have to choose.

ATTACKER.title: Hold as the call changes
ATTACKER.body:
Stop attacking just before the call changes: a hit with the wrong style hurts you.

The overlay tells you when to stop. To stop, click an empty tile on the ground.

ATTACKER.title: Nothing to attack
ATTACKER.body:
Once the Fighters and Rangers are all dead, help at the egg launcher.

Click the launcher when the overlay asks, then click the button that BA Autopilot outlines in its window.

ATTACKER.title: Low HP: the hill
ATTACKER.body:
When your health is low, the overlay sends you onto a launcher hill. Penance can't follow you up there.

Walk up the hill and ask your Healer for the vial. Go back once you're healed.

ATTACKER.title: Wave 10: spikes
ATTACKER.body:
In wave 10, take spikes from a petrified mushroom: click the mushroom. The overlay asks you to do this before the Queen appears.

When the Healer passes you a poisoned egg, click the spikes in your inventory, then click the poisoned egg. Then pass the spiked egg to the Defender: click it, then click the Defender.

ATTACKER.title: Wave 10: waiting
ATTACKER.body: Leave the Queen alone: weapons can't hurt her. Wait by the Healer spring for the next poisoned egg.

ATTACKER.title: Attacker: done
ATTACKER.body: That's the Attacker. Click Defender > to continue with the Defender tutorial.

DEFENDER.title: Before you start
DEFENDER.body:
The Defender is probably the hardest role to get started with. Try to get a good idea of the minigame first, for example by playing the other roles.

The Defender also benefits a lot from acting quickly at the start of each wave: the faster you drop the bait pattern, the better the Runners are led to the trap.

DEFENDER.title: The Defender
DEFENDER.body:
As the Defender, you lure the Penance Runners onto the trap with the bait the Healer calls, and you repair the trap when it breaks. You also tell the Healer which poisoned food to use.

BA Autopilot shows you one step at a time: where to drop bait, when to repair the trap, and when a Runner is escaping. It colours the right call green in your horn's menu.

DEFENDER.title: The BA Autopilot overlay
DEFENDER.body:
This is the BA Autopilot overlay. It shows the one thing to do now. You can move it by holding Alt and dragging it.

The coloured tag shows what kind of step it is. Under it are your call, the call you heard, and the time left before the next call.

DEFENDER.title: Your call
DEFENDER.body:
Every 30 seconds, the Healer needs a new call from you: which poisoned food to use. When it's time, your game view turns red. That's your signal.

*Stop whatever you're doing.* Right-click your horn and pick the Tell- option that BA Autopilot colours green. The red goes away once you've called.

DEFENDER.title: Opening: Stock-Up
DEFENDER.body: Start at your dispenser. Click it once: its left-click is Stock-Up, which gives you all three kinds of bait in one go.

DEFENDER.title: Good bait and its range
DEFENDER.body:
Runners only notice bait that is close to them: within 4 tiles, or 5 tiles from Defender level 2. On the ground, BA Autopilot outlines the tiles around each bait where a Runner notices it.

Good bait is the bait the Healer called. A Runner that notices good bait walks to it and eats it. If the bait is on the trap's food tile, the trap kills the Runner while it eats.

A bait counts as good or bad by the call at the moment it hits the ground, so wait for the Healer's call before you drop it.

DEFENDER.title: Bad bait
DEFENDER.body:
Bad bait is any bait the Healer didn't call. A Runner that notices bad bait walks to it, eats it, and then runs several tiles north.

That makes bad bait useful too: drop it in a Runner's way to send it north, back towards the trap. The bait pattern uses a few bad baits for this.

DEFENDER.title: Good and bad bait
DEFENDER.body: Your inventory marks each bait as GOOD or BAD for the current call. Good bait is the one the Healer called.

DEFENDER.title: The bait pattern
DEFENDER.body:
In the first call, drop bait on the marked tiles. Each tile shows how much good or bad bait it needs.

To drop bait, stand on the tile, then click the bait in your inventory: its left-click is Drop. Good bait pulls Runners to the trap, and bad bait sends them north. *Drop it early.*

DEFENDER.title: Logs and hammer
DEFENDER.body: Then pick up the hammer and the logs in one trip: click each of them on the ground. You need them to repair the trap.

DEFENDER.title: Runner outlines
DEFENDER.body:
Runners are outlined by how well your bait holds them: green when they're stacked on the trap, light green when lured to good bait, yellow near bad bait only, orange when loose, and red when escaping.

Don't stand on the trap's food tile: Runners can't eat it while you're on it. The overlay marks the tile to step onto.

DEFENDER.title: Repairing the trap
DEFENDER.body:
After two kills, the trap breaks. You need logs and the hammer in your inventory to fix it.

Stand on the food tile and click the trap. With logs and the hammer, its left-click is Fix.

DEFENDER.title: Escaping runners
DEFENDER.body:
A Runner that gets past the trap is escaping, and an escape costs your team points.

*Get ahead of it:* walk to the marked tile. Then click a bad bait in your inventory to drop it: the Runner eats it and runs north, back towards the trap.

DEFENDER.title: Restocking
DEFENDER.body: Runners eat the bait. When a tile runs out, the overlay sends you to drop more there, the same way as before.

DEFENDER.title: All Runners dead
DEFENDER.body: Once every Runner is dead, the overlay asks you to hide behind the corner east of the trap, so the Penance Healers stay by the wall. Then help at the egg launcher: click it, then click the button BA Autopilot outlines in its window.

DEFENDER.title: Wave 10: lava crater
DEFENDER.body:
In wave 10, the Attacker passes you spiked eggs. With a spiked egg in your inventory, click a lava crater: the egg becomes an omega egg.

Then pass the omega egg to the Collector: click it in your inventory, then click the Collector.

DEFENDER.title: Wave 10: waiting
DEFENDER.body: Leave the Queen alone: weapons can't hurt her. Wait by the Healer spring for the next spiked egg.

DEFENDER.title: Defender: done
DEFENDER.body: That's the Defender, and all four roles. You're ready for a run: BA Autopilot will guide you through each wave.
